nodes.title: Lower Limb Nerve Lesions
nodes.body:
• 1: All ankle and foot actions weak. Preserved Medial leg sensation, all other sensation ↓.
  • 2: FOOT DROP (↓ dorsiflexion) + ↓EVERSION. ↓ LATERAL LEG and DORSUM OF FOOT sensation.
  • 3: ↓EVERSION + ↓ dorsum of foot sensation. DORSIFLEXION IS SPARED!
  • 4: FOOT DROP (↓ dorsiflexion), ↓ sensation b/w. 1-2ND TOES only. EVERSION IS SPARED!
  • 5: ↓ PLANTAR FLEXION (↓ TOE WALK), ↓ plantar foot sensation.
  • 6: L5 RADICULOPATHY - ↓HIP ABDUCTION, ↓ Dorsiflexion, ↓ Dorsum of foot sensation.
  • 7: S1 RADICULOPATHY - ↓PLANTAR FLEXION, ↓ Achilles Tendon Reflex, ↓ lateral/plantar foot sensation.
  • ↳ Test radiculopathies using myotome + dermatome testing.

nodes.title: Memory Trick for Dermatomes + Myotomes (Lower Limb)
nodes.body:
• Work back from the ones you never forget: L3 dermatome + S1 myotome.
  • Dermatomes (green underline): Start at medial knee (L3) → medial ankle (L4) → Dorsum of foot (L5) → Lateral - plantar foot (S1)
  • Myotomes (orange underline): Start w. foot plantar flexion (S1) → Foot dorsiflexion (L5) → Knee extension (L4) → Hip flexion (L3)

nodes.title: Fractures
nodes.body:

nodes.title: Salter Harris Fractures

nodes.title: Other Pediatric Ortho Dx
nodes.body:
• Club Feet
  • Normal Genu Varum (0-2 y.o.), genu valgum (3-7 y.o.), in/out toes (-15° to 15°)
  • Scoliosis (Idiopathic, rarely w. pain)

nodes.title: Pediatric Hip Disorders
nodes.body:
• (CHILD WITH A LIMP)
  • Developmental dysplasia of the hip (Barlow and Ortolani Tests)
  • Legg Calve Perthes Disease (Idiopathic AVN of femur head, ↑ in school-age kids)
  • Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis ❗ (Idiopathic growth plate Dx → Slipped head → AVN w.o Sx)
  • Non-accidental injury (abuse, ex. Femur fracture in < 1 y.o.)
  • TRANSIENT SYNOVITIS (Post-URTI, self-resolves)
    • ↳ Rule out Septic Arthritis

nodes.title: Paediatric Rheumatology: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
nodes.body:
• Invx: ↑CRP + ESR, CBC, ANA (for uveitis risk), RF, HLA B27. X-rays (↑ joint maturation w. leg length discrepancy → Growth arrest).
  • Complications: Growth disturbances, ↓function, ANTERIOR UVEITIS: ↑ risk if ANA +ve ∴ screen often. May lead to blindness.

nodes.title: 6 JIA Subtypes
nodes.body:
• 1. OLIGOARTHRITIS ♀: ↑ in 2-4 y.o. Tx w. NSAIDs
  • 2. POLYARTHRITIS ♀: RF -ve in younger kids. RF +ve in teens, PEx + Tx similar to adult RA.
  • 3. ENTHESITIS-RELATED JIA ♂: PEx + Tx similar to adult ankylosing spondylitis.
  • 4. PSORIATIC JIA ♀: Similar to adult PsA.
  • 5. Undifferentiated JIA
  • 6. SYSTEMIC JIA aka STILL'S DISEASE: More serious and life threatening JIA.
    • Salmon-colored RASH
    • Jalapeño (hot) - FEVERS
    • I - "Eye" - UVEITIS + Systemic s/s
    • A - ARTHRITIS ± effusion.
  • Complication in SJIA: MACROPHAGE ACTIVATION SYNDROME
  • Tx: NSAIDs, steroids. If fever present: IL-1 + IL-6 BLOCKER
    • tx uveitis w. methotrexate → Anti-TNF Inhibitors

nodes.title: Hand Cellulitis
nodes.body:
• Pathophys: Staph Aureus or G.A. Strep. → Superficial Skin infection.
  • PEx: Inflam. s/s (Erythema, hot, swelling, tender) often in DORSAL side, wrist to MCP, w. irregular margins.
  • Tx: ABx (Keflex/Cephalexin)

nodes.title: Abscess
nodes.body:
• Deep space Infections
  • PALMAR Surface
  • PARONYCHIA (Nail)
  • FELON (Pulp space)
  • Joints and tendons
    • ↳ Tx: ABx, INCISION + DRAINAGE, wound care

nodes.title: Diabetic Foot Infections
nodes.body:
• (Review PoM II - Endo: Diabetes)
  • DM → ↓ IMMUNITY via multiple MOA, MICRO- and MACRO-VASCULAR dx ↑ risk of foot lesions.
  • Classif.: Staph Aureus cellulitis (Mild)
    • Deep space (>2cm) infection + OM (Moderate)
    • → OM + Sepsis: SIRS criteria (Severe)

notes.name: Clinical approach to the ankle and foot

nodes.title: MSK Infections
nodes.body:
• (Review FoM - Microbio: Staph Aureus + GAS)
  • Others: Bursitis, myositis, necrotizing fasciitis.

nodes.title: Osteomyelitis
nodes.body:
• Most commonly STAPH AUREUS (Adherence/BIOFILMS and Immune evasion intracellularly in osteoblasts)
  • Invx: CBC, CRP, BLOOD CULTURES + imaging:
    • MRI is most sensitive (especially for VOM).
    • X-ray + CT NOT sensitive enough!
  • Acute OM → Inflammation → Vascular Congestion and small vessel THROMBOSIS → NECROSIS of cortical bone → No blood supply = ABx cannot reach site (↑ RECURRENCE)
    • ∴ CHRONIC OM is difficult to treat
  • Tx w. higher doses of IV ABx ± Surgical debridement

nodes.title: Follow-Up OM Invx
nodes.body:
• MRI will show persistent OM findings despite resolution.
    • ∴ DO NOT REPEAT MRI if pt. is clinically improving.
  • Invx OM RELAPSE with NM tagged WBC Scan.

nodes.title: Pediatric Osteomyelitis
nodes.body:
• Organisms: S. Aureus. If Sickle Cell Dx (↓ blood flow + asplenia = ↓ immunity) ↑ risk of Salmonella OM. Gram Negs.
  • Commonly in metaphysis → vascular region ∴ easier to tx than adults.

nodes.title: Vertebral Osteomyelitis (VOM)
nodes.body:
• Organisms: Most are STAPH AUREUS. Suspect TB if Hx of travel ex. India (TB → VOM = POTT'S DISEASE)
  • Complications: Paravertebral abscess, EPIDURAL ABSCESS (Compress spinal cord) ❗
    • ↳ Urgent Neurosurgery

notes.name: Clinical approach to non-mechanical back and neck pain

nodes.title: Non-Gonococcal
nodes.body:
• STAPH AUREUS (MSSA or MRSA) + STREPTOCOCCUS (GAS) most common.
  • LYME DISEASE ex. Hx of Hiking/Camping
    • or TB ex. India immig.

nodes.title: Gonococcal
nodes.body:
• (Nisseria GONORRHEA STI)
  • ↑ in YOUNG pt, multiple sex partners

nodes.title: Infectious Polyarthritis
nodes.body:
• Bacterial (ex. Staph Aureus): ↑ Risk of INFECTIOUS ENDOCARDITIS. May have MURMUR on PEx.
  • Often VIRAL ex. Parvo B-19, HIV, Chikungunya, Zika, Dengue, Hep B C

nodes.title: Disseminated Gonococcal Disease
nodes.body:
• PEx Triad:
    • POLYARTHRALGIAS (Migratory + Asymmetric)
    • TENOSYNOVITIS
    • Dermatitis w. PUSTULAR RASH

nodes.title: Infection vs. Inflammation
nodes.body:
• BLOODWORK
  • Signs of ACUTE INFECTION:
    • ↑↑ CRP (and ESR)
    • WBC Count >10,000 (often neutrophils)
    • ↑↑ Plt (Reactive Thrombocytosis)
    • Normal Hgb
  • NORMAL VALUES (dashed box):
    • WBC <10,000
    • CRP <3
    • Plt 150 - 400
    • Hbg 120-160
  • Signs of CHRONIC INFLAMMATION:
    • ↑ CRP (and ESR)
    • Normal WBC count, may be modest ↑ (often monocytes, lymphocytes)
    • ↑ Plt: Reactive Thrombocytosis
    • ↓ Hgb: Anemia of chronic inflamm.
  • PHYSICAL EXAM:
    • Tumor (Swelling/effusion)
    • Dolor (Pain/Tender)
    • Functio Laesa (↓ ROM)
  • More common w. infection:
    • Calor (Hot on palpation)
    • Rubor (Erythema/red)
    • Fever + Malaise
    • ↑RR + ↑HR

nodes.title: Post-Infection Joint Pain
nodes.body:
• + Persistent systemic signs (ex. Fever) + CBC + inflamm. markers: Consider BACTEREMIA + Hematogenous Seeding
  • 1-3 wks after Urinary or GI tract Infection w. red eyes, dysuria, and arthralgia w. ↑CRP + ESR
  • 1 week after infection (often URTI) + No systemic signs + No CBC Inflamm. markers
  • Post-untreated STREP (G.A.S) Infection

nodes.title: Transient Synovitis
nodes.body: • Self-resolves.

nodes.title: Acute Rheumatic Fever
nodes.body:
• Post G.A.S (ex. Pharyngitis)
  • Recall "Jones" criteria
    • Migratory Arthritis
  • (Review PoM I - Cardio: Valvular Disease)

nodes.title: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis
nodes.body:
• Nephritic syndrome → RPGN
  • (Review PoM I - Nephro)

nodes.title: Lupus (SLE) Glomerulonephritis
nodes.body:
• ❗ (heading)
  • (Review PoM I - Nephrology Map 2)
  • Pathophys: Immune complex deposits in GBM → NEPHRITIC SYNDROME → RPGN → AKI
  • PEx: HEMATURIA, edema, oliguria...
  • Invx: LOW COMPLEMENT (C3, C4) due to overconsumption. Urinalysis w. RBC CASTS
  • Tx: HIGH-DOSE PREDNISONE ❗

nodes.title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)
nodes.body:
• (old age) ♀
  • Keywords: THROMBOSIS (ex. DVT), recurrent MISCARRIAGES, LIVEDO RETICULARIS
  • Etiology: 1° - Idiopathic, 50% are 2° to SLE, 2° to other dx (RA, HIV, Hep...)
  • Pathophys: Anti-phospholipid antibodies → Inflamm. damage to cell membranes ex. ENDOTHELIAL cells, Anti-phos. Ab bind to platelets → ↑ PLATELET ACTIVATION → Activate coagulation cascade → HYPERCOAGULATION, THROMBOSIS in arteries (ex. Brain) + veins (ex. DVT)
  • PEx: Thrombosis → Placental infarction → women w. RECURRENT MISCARRIAGES.
    • Thrombotic events - DVT, PE, MI, STROKE. Venous microthrombi in skin - backup of blood under skin - LIVEDO RETICULARIS.
  • Invx: Similar to SLE but ↓Plt (overconsumption), ± Hemolytic Anemia (↑LDH, ↑Bili...)
    • Antibodies: LUPUS ANTICOAGULANT, Anti-cardiolipin (Causes False +ve VDRL) ± SLE Abs.
    • Coagulation Panel: Lupus anticoagulant is an anticoagulant IN VITRO ∴ ↑PTT (+does not correct w. mixing study), but IN VIVO it activates platelets ∴ PRO-THROMBOTIC
    • (Review FoM I - Thrombotic Disorders)
  • Tx: ASA (Anti-platelet), WARFARIN, HEPARIN. If pregnant: ASA + LMWH. + avoid meds high in estrogen (↑thrombosis risk)

nodes.title: Raynaud's Phenomenon
nodes.body:
• (Most commonly due to SCLERODERMA)
  • Etiology: 1° Idiopathic (Common, no other CT dx s/s, benign). 2° to CT diseases. 95% of SSc pt. have Raynaud's.
  • Pathophys + PEx: Inflammation of arterioles + capillaries + cold temperature trigger → Vasospasm in the digits of hands + feet → ↓ blood flow begins TRIPHASIC PEx (All in 10-20 mins) →
    • Ischemia: WHITE/pallor fingers/toes → Hypoxia at site: BLUE/cyanosis fingers/toes → ↓O2 in tunica media stops vasoconstriction → Reactive Hyperemia/Blood re-enters: RED fingers/toes.
  • Complications: Chronic ischemic damage → Finger pulp atrophy, digital ulcerations, gangrene.
  • Tx: Avoid triggers (Cold, BBs, smoking, stress), CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS (ex. Nifedipine) or other vasodilators.

nodes.title: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
nodes.body: • Has features of SLE + polymyositis + scleroderma

nodes.title: Acetaminophen
nodes.body:
• Analgesic but not anti-inflammatory.
  • Tx of OA, mild relief.

nodes.title: Colchicine
nodes.body:
• Immunosuppresant.
    • (↓Mitosis → ↓Cell Proliferation → ↓Immune cells)
  • Tx of GOUT

nodes.title: NSAIDs
nodes.body:
• (↓Prostaglandins via COX-2 ± COX-1)
  • ↓pain and swelling but do NOT prevent RA disease progression, do not delay erosions.
    • ∴ are NOT DISEASE MODIFYING drugs.
  • Relative contraindications: CVD, GI disease, Renal Dx. (CI if end-stage CKD). Screening Invx (CBC, ALT, Cr)
  • Two subtypes:
    • COX-2 SELECTIVE: CELECOXIB (↓ GI toxicity)
    • NON-SELECTIVE: IBUPROFEN, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Indomethacin

nodes.title: NSAID Side Effects
nodes.body:
• Renal insufficiency
  • CVD: HTN, MI, CVA

nodes.title: Steroids
nodes.body:
• (ex. PREDNISONE)
  • Dosage: High-dose (1mg/kg) for life threatening dx: ANCA-vasculitis, lupus nephritis, Giant Cell Arteritis + Polymyositis/Dermatomyositis ❗
    • Med-dose (up to 40mg) for acute flares of RA, PMR and acute gout flare
    • Low-dose (<5mg) used chronically if DMARDs or biologics not tolerated.
  • Relative Contraindications: Diabetes, CVD, Osteoporosis, Infections, Cataracts.

nodes.title: Steroid Side Effects
nodes.body: • ∴ Taper-off and if chronic Tx needed use "STEROID-SPARING" meds: DMARDs or Biologics

nodes.title: Gastritis
nodes.body:
• (+ PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE)
  • Prophylaxis with PROTEIN-PUMP INHIBITOR

nodes.title: Osteoporosis
nodes.body:
• (Review PoM II - Endo: Calcium Homeostasis)
  • Prophylaxis w. CALCIUM + VITAMIN D Supplements for acute or chronic Tx.
    • + BIPHOSPHONATES if chronic Tx.
  • If inadequate prophylaxis: ↓osteocytes → ↓blood supply → ↑risk of FRACTURES → AVASCULAR NECROSIS

nodes.title: Others (steroid side effects)
nodes.body:
• (↑ if chronic steroids)
  • CUSHING'S SYNDROME
  • ↑ risk of infections
  • Hyperglycemia + Diabetes
  • Psych. changes
  • Cataracts + Glaucoma
  • Hypertension, CVD.

nodes.title: DMARDs
nodes.body:
• (DISEASE MODIFYING ANTI-RHEUMATIC DRUGS)
  • Start EARLY in RA to ↓ disease progression since rate of erosions is highest in first 2 years.
  • Use TRIPLE THERAPY (Comb. of agents) + TREAT TO TARGET: ↑ dose q.3-6 months until no swollen/tender joints.
  • Monitor monthly w. CBC, ALT, Cr, CRP for SIDE EFFECTS. ex. GHMI (GI upset, hepatotoxic, myelosup/cytopenia, infections)

nodes.title: Methotrexate
nodes.body:
• Side Effects: GHMI + oral ulcer, PNEUMONITIS, teratogenic.
  • Use w. FOLIC ACID weekly. Avoid alcohol + Sulfa ABx.

nodes.title: Hydroxychloroquine
nodes.body:
• Side Effects: RETINAL TOXICITY (Bull's Eye Maculopathy). ↓visual acuity, Skin rash, GI upset, Headache. No myelosupression.
  • Monitor with ANNUAL EYE EXAMINATION. No bloodwork.

nodes.title: Others (DMARDs)
nodes.body:
• SULFASALAZINE: Similar side effects as MTX + CNS, rash, oligospermia
  • LEFLUNOMIDE: GHMI + HTN, Peripheral neuropathy, PNEUMONITIS

nodes.title: Biologics
nodes.body: • (ex. Anti-TNFα, IL-1 or IL-6 common)

nodes.title: TNF Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• (ex. Infliximab)
  • Contraindications: Active, recent or recurrent infection, active cancer, MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (or FHx) or class III/IV CHF

nodes.title: Sarcomas
nodes.body:
• Malignant SOFT TISSUE tumor: liposarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma (smooth muscle), fibrosarcoma, neurofibrosarcoma
  • Etiology: most are IDIOPATHIC. Very rare.
    • vs. BENIGN soft tissue tumors are common, ex. LIPOMAS
  • PEx: LUMP & rapid growth, pain, DEEP and FIXED.
  • Invx: If <5cm: EXCISE. If >5cm: Imaging (MRI or CT) → CORE BIOPSY → Histopathology & histochemical studies.
  • Staging Invx: CT scan (lung mets most common)
  • Tx: Multidisciplinary team - Pre-op RADIATION → Sx resection. No adjuvant chemo.

  • Deep Posterior - Popliteus, Tibialis Posterior (FOOT INVERSION), Flexor Digitorum Longus & Flexor Hallucis Longus (TOE FLEXION) and assist in PLANTAR FLEXION

nodes.title: Neck & Back Pain
nodes.body:
• (SPONDY = Vertebrae)
  • Muscular mechanical pain ex. strains, myofascial pain

nodes.title: Neck
nodes.body:

  • Cervical Radiculopathy w. positive Spurling's maneuver
  • Cervical central canal stenosis: Cervical Myelopathy ❗

nodes.title: Low Back
nodes.body:
• Hip/Buttock Pain mimicking low back pain: SI joint dysfunction, piriformis syndrome...
  • Lumbar Radiculopathy
  • Lumbar central canal stenosis (Similar to lumbar radic.)
  • Severe Lumbar central canal stenosis: Cauda Equina Syndrome ❗

nodes.title: Back Pain Red Flags
nodes.body:
• NEUROLOGIC Back Pain (Cervical Myelopathy, Cauda Equina Syndrome)
  • INFLAMMATORY Spine Pain ex. Ankylosing Spondylitis
  • FRACTURES ex. Osteoporosis Vertebral Compression Fracture, Spondylolysis
  • INFECTIONS ex. Osteomyelitis, Epidural Abscess
  • NEOPLASM ex. Renal carcinoma referred pain, prostate cancer metastasis
  • VASCULAR: Neck - vertebral artery insufficiency, Low back - Distal Claudication (Lumbar Stenosis)
  • VISCERAL: AAA, MI, PUD, Pancreatitis, other GI, Pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, OB/GYN

nodes.title: Shoulder
nodes.body:
• Shoulder joint Instability/Separation
  • Rotator Cuff Syndrome - End Stage Arthropathy
  • Rotator Cuff Syndrome (Tendinopathy) } ACTIVE ROM restricted, passive ROM preserved
  • Shoulder Rheumatoid Arthritis
  • Shoulder Osteoarthritis
  • Adhesive Capsulitis
    • (Shoulder OA + Adhesive capsulitis) } Restrict BOTH active & passive ROM
  • Proximal Biceps Tendinopathy
  • Erb's Palsy (Waiter's Tip Sign)
  • Proximal Humerus Fracture w. Axillary N. Palsy
  • Winged Scapula
  • Supraspinatus or Deltoid Atrophy

nodes.title: Hip
nodes.body:
• Referred back pain (Lumbar Radiculopathy)
  • OA of the hip (Morning Stiffness)
  • Femoroacetabular Impingement
  • Labral Tear
  • Hip fractures
  • Avascular Necrosis of Femoral Head
    • (OA of hip through AVN) } Anterior/Groin Pain
  • Deep Gluteal Syndrome ex. Piriformis Syndrome (worsens w. prolonged sitting)
  • Sacroiliac joint dysfunction (ex. Post-Pregnancy) w. +ve FABER test.
    • (Deep gluteal + SI joint) } Posterior pain (Mimics Low Back Pain)
  • Greater trochanteric pain syndrome - lateral pain, worse w. lying on side (w. Trendelenburg Sign)

nodes.title: Summary of Antibiotics
nodes.body:
• Staph Aureus & GAS (Cellulitis, Septic Arthritis): IV Cefazolin (Ancef) or P.O. Cephalexin (Keflex)
    • If MRSA risk (IVDU, Hospital): Vancomycin + Ceftriaxone
  • If Pseudomonas or severe infection: Pip-Tazo

nodes.title: Suppurative Tenosynovitis
nodes.body:
• Pathophys: Skin injury → Staph Aureus or GAS in deep tissue → TENDON SHEATH infection.
  • RFs: DIABETES, RA, ↓immunity, IVDU.
  • PEx: KANAVEL'S 4 CARDINAL SIGNS
    • 1. Swelling of entire finger
    • 2. Flexion posture
    • 3. Tender along tendon sheath
    • 4. Intense pain w. extension

nodes.title: Hand Septic Arthritis
nodes.body:
• Pathophys: Cat bites (Pasteurella) → PIP and DIP
  • Human "bites" (mixed flora/E. corrodens) → MCP infection

nodes.title: Vasculitis
nodes.body:
• SYSTEMIC inflammation: Systemic symptoms (ex. fevers, weight loss)
  • Inflammation & OCCLUSION of arterial wall: tissue ISCHEMIA & multi-organ symptoms ± PURPURA (Non-blancheable rash) !
  • (2° branch) May be 2° to INFECTIONS (Hep B/C, HIV, TB...), cancer, drugs (ex. cocaine), CT dx (SLE, RA, SS...). All need to be ruled out prior to Tx of 1° dx.

nodes.title: Giant Cell Arteritis
nodes.body:
• ❗ (old age) ♀
  • aka TEMPORAL ARTERITIS
  • Keywords: >70 y.o. new TEMPLE HEADACHE, PMR HIP & SHOULDER PAIN
  • Pathophys: Age + genetics → Systemic inflammation & PMR → Macrophages attracted to wall of LARGE ARTERIES (preference for CAROTID A. branches) → Macrophages fuse inside wall, form GIANT CELLS (can be biopsied for dx) → Vascular damage → Abnormal ↑ wall thickness → Occlusion → Tissue HYPOXIA
  • PEx: ONLY OLDER Pt. >50 y.o., most are >70 y.o.
    • Inflamm. of Sup. Temporal A.: New TEMPORAL HEADACHES, tender scalp. Temporal A. swollen, firm, nodular, tender & may be non-pulsatile. JAW claudication.
    • Inflamm. of OPHTHALMIC A.: Diplopia, and vision loss (usually one eye first) → BLINDNESS ❗, TIA or STROKES. Systemic S/S.
  • Invx: ↑CRP & ESR: If -ve, rule out GCA. If +ve (w. GCA S/S) - START TREATMENT (ASAP) → Urgent referral for TEMPORAL ARTERY BIOPSY (or doppler U/S) for diagnosis.
    • Note: GCA causes skip lesions ∴ biopsy at multiple sites (-ve biopsy does NOT rule out GCA)
  • Tx: HIGH DOSE PREDNISONE (ASAP to prevent blindness)

nodes.title: Kawasaki Disease
nodes.body:
• PEx: "CRASH & Burn"
  • (Review FoM - Microbiology)

nodes.title: Henoch-Schönlein Purpura
nodes.body:
• aka IgA Nephropathy
  • (Review PoM I - Nephro Map 2)

nodes.title: ANCA-Associated Vasculitis
nodes.body:
• ❗
  • (Review PoM I - Nephro: Nephritic Syndrome)
  • PEx: Painful NON-BLANCHEABLE rash (PURPURA), skin ulcers, SINUSITIS: bloody discharge/crusting, ARTHRITIS (inflamm.) & HEMATURIA, Pulmonary nodules/embolism/bleed w. DYSPNEA, B-SYMP.
    • vs DDx for PURPURA includes COAGULOPATHY: Invx w. INR, PTT (↑) or ↓Plt.
  • Invx: ↑CRP & ESR, ↑Plt, ↓Hg, Renal: Cr, Urinalysis & RBC CASTS, Lung: Chest X-RAY (NODULES)
    • RULE OUT 2° vasculitis (WBC, cultures, LFT, Hep B/C, HIV, VDRL. Invx cancer - Serum Protein Electrop.) →
  • BIOPSY, Immunofluorescence to detect ANCA = Anti-Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody. Granules are either cytoplasmic (C-ANCA) or perinuclear (P-ANCA). -ve does not rule out.
    • vs ANCA FALSE +ve due to INFECTIONS, cancer, meds & cocaine. ↑PANCA and cANCA together ↑ suspicion of COCAINE-INDUCED VASCULITIS.
  • Complications: Pulmonary Hemorrhage, ANCA-Associated GLOMERULONEPHRITIS (may progress to RPGN → AKI) ❗
  • Tx: HIGH-DOSE PREDNISONE (After infections ruled out). Admit if not stable.

nodes.title: C-ANCA Vasculitis
nodes.body:
• Granulomatosis w. Polyangiitis (GPA) aka Wegener's Disease
  • PEx w. "Saddle Nose Deformity"

nodes.title: P-ANCA Vasculitis
nodes.body:
• Microscopic Polyangiitis (MPA)
  • Eosinophilic GPA (EGPA) aka Churg-Strauss Syndrome

nodes.title: Therapeutic Arthrocentesis & Steroid Injections
nodes.body:
• Complications: infection, bleeding, fat atrophy, tendon rupture.
    • + for steroid injections: Systemic absorption, post-injection flare.
  • Steroid Injection contraindications: SEPTIC JOINT, overlying skin infection or psoriasis, PROSTHETIC joint, bleeding disorder, allergy to anest.
  • ∴ Need to RULE OUT SEPTIC JOINT w. arthrocentesis before steroid injections

nodes.title: Acute Monoarthritis
nodes.body:
• PEx: "Acute HOT and RED JOINT"
  • All can present w. systemic S/S (ex. FEVER)
  • Initial Invx: ARTHROCENTESIS
    • Synovial fluid analysis of "3Cs/C3G": Cell Count, Culture + Gram Stain + Crystals
    • (Also THERAPEUTIC since ↓swelling & pain)

nodes.title: Septic Arthritis
nodes.body:
• ❗ (children) (old age)
  • RFs: Travel, unsafe sex, IVDU, DM, RA, ↓immunity, PROSTHETICS (↑biofilms), ↓↓ or ↑age.
  • Pathophys: STAPH AUREUS & G.A.S (see etiologies) → HEMATOGENOUS SEEDING or direct inoculation → Acute synovitis & purulent effusion → Inflamm. damage to joint.
  • PEx: Acute "Hot, red, swollen, tender" joint, ↓ROM, systemic signs - FEVER!
  • Invx: ARTHROCENTESIS synovial fluid w. >50,000 WBCs (Mostly NEUTROPHILS), synovial fluid and BLOOD CULTURE & GRAM STAIN, CBC, lytes, Cr, CRP & U/S, X-ray.
  • Tx: Refer to ortho for SURGERY (Joint decompression, irrigation & debridement)
    • ABx - For Staph Aureus + GAS: IV CEFAZOLIN ("Ancef"). If MRSA risk (IVDU, Hospital exposure) VANCO + Ceftriaxone. Adjust based on C+S. ABx for 4-6 wks.

nodes.title: Gout
nodes.body:
• ♂ (old age)
  • Keywords: BIG TOE, ALCOHOL
  • RFs: ↑Purine intake (Red meat, fish, alcohol), chemo (tumor lysis syndrome), CKD, genetics, Thyroid Dx, Metabolic syndrome (HTN, DM...), HTN meds (Thiazide & Loop Diuretics - ↑urea reabs.)
  • Pathophys: ↑URIC ACID → Crystallization → Deposits in tissues → Inflammation rxn to crystal
  • PEx: Trigger (ex. Binge drinking) → Acute "red, hot, swollen, tender" joint, classically 1st MTP (PODAGRA)
    • CHRONIC gout may present w. TOPHI - Crystals in skin.
  • Invx: Arthrocentesis w. NEEDLE-shaped CRYSTALS, (-) birefringence under polarized light (YELLOW under parallel light). Normal X-ray, CBC maybe w. ↑WBC, Plt. Invx cause - TSH, Cr, OGTT, LDL, Uric Acid (May be low during attack, HYPERURICEMIA ≠ Gout dx)
  • Tx: Ed, RICE, lifestyle, NSAIDs or COXIBs, COLCHICINE, Medium Dose PREDNISONE (short-term)
    • If recurrent attacks or tophi, treat w: ALLOPURINOL ! (Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor)
    • Note that starting or stopping allopurinol triggers an acute flare, ∴ need prophylaxis w. NSAIDs or Colchicine
    • Requires LIFELONG use.
    • (Review FoM - Leukemia: Tumor Lysis Syndrome)

nodes.title: Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR)
nodes.body:
• ♀ (old age)
  • Keywords: HIP/SHOULDER PAIN w. NO WEAKNESS, FAST RESPONSE TO PREDNISONE.
  • RFs: GIANT CELL TEMPORAL ARTERITIS ∴ ↑risk of blindness. ↑AGE.
  • Pathophys: Poorly understood. ↑immune response → Systemic inflammation (NOT involving muscle)
  • MSK PEx: Insidious onset bilateral PROXIMAL (HIP + SHOULDER) PAIN + STIFFNESS (but NOT weakness). Stiffness worse in MORNING. Other than pain, examination of joints is normal.
  • Systemic PEx: FATIGUE + WEIGHT LOSS ± fevers, night sweats (B-symptoms, rule out neoplasm)
  • Invx: ↑CRP, ↑ESR: ↓Hgb, ↑Plt. ∴ INFLAMMATORY but NORMAL CK. No specific autoantibodies ex. -ve RF. Imaging w. joint + bursae inflammation but NORMAL MUSCLES. Rule out other dx. Often clinical diagnosis.
  • Tx: Medium-dose PREDNISONE (Taper off throughout 2yrs) - VERY FAST (48 hrs) PMR S/S IMPROVEMENT!
    • No other dx improves as fast + dramatically as PMR w. steroids. If no response in 1 week, consider alternate dx.

nodes.title: Non-Inflammatory aka Arthralgia
nodes.body: • = Joint pain with no inflammation.

nodes.title: Non-Articular
nodes.body:
• Generalized: Inflammatory or Non-inflammatory
  • Localized: Bursitis, Tendinitis, Capsulitis, Muscle Sprain

nodes.title: Joint Pain
nodes.body: • Recall articular CARTILAGE does NOT regenerate: Damage due to chronic degeneration or autoimmune inflammation is IRREVERSIBLE. (boxed note, dashed to Articular)

nodes.title: Arthritis
nodes.body: • (Joint Inflammation)

nodes.title: Fibromyalgia
nodes.body:
• ♀ (adults)
  • Keywords: PAIN EVERYWHERE, NO INFLAMMATION
  • RFs: Comorbid CNS Dx (ex. SLEEP, mood) and SOMATIC dx (ex. IBS)
  • Pathophys: Poorly understood. CENTRAL SENSITIZATION to pain, ↓inhibitory pathway (NE, 5HT), ↑facilitatory pathway (Glutamate, Subs. P).
  • MSK PEx: DIFFUSE CENTRAL PAIN (ex. hurts everywhere, bothered by light) w. "tender points", neuropathic pain (numb, burning) but NO muscle weakness
  • Systemic PEx: Headache, FATIGUE, cognitive changes ("FIBRO FOG"), ↓sleep.
  • Invx: NORMAL ESR + CRP. No autoantibodies. No X-ray/MRI findings.
  • Diagnosis: ≥3 MONTHS of pain + 4/5 regions of generalized pain + min. points on questionnaire (Widespread pain index + symptom severity). NOT a dx of exclusion: i.e. common to dx FM AND other dx (ex. FM + RA). Dx by Family Doctor.
  • Tx: EXERCISE, Antidepressants: SNRI (ex. DULOXETINE!), TCA (Amitriptyline), neuropathic pain meds (ex. Gabapentin, pregabalin). AVOID OPIOIDS.

nodes.title: Centralizing Pain
nodes.body:
• Disturbance in pain processing resulting in HYPERALGESIA, Sensitivity to light, noise, odor, and light pressure (ex. pain w. clothes)
  • Responds to drugs that alter pain NTs. Does NOT respond to opioids

nodes.title: Degenerative Arthritis
nodes.body:
• PEx: Pain w. MOTION, Morning STIFFNESS <30 mins
  • Invx: X-RAYS + rule out other dx
  • Diagnosis is CLINICAL
  • 1°: IDIOPATHIC (Most common)
  • 2°: Metabolic (ex. HyperPTH), hemophilic, Neuropathic (ex. 2° to Diabetes), POST-TRAUMATIC OA (ex. ACL tear)

nodes.title: Osteoarthritis
nodes.body:
• ♀ (old age)
  • (CHRONIC MONOARTHRITIS or asymmetric polyarthritis)
  • Keywords: OLDER, trauma, DIP, ↑w. activity.
  • RFs: ↑AGE, obesity, overuse, Hx of TRAUMA, FHx (genetics)
  • Pathophys: Chronic stress on joint → Inflammation/degeneration of all joint tissues → Articular CARTILAGE DESTRUCTION, aberrant BONE DEPOSITION (OSTEOPHYTES, Subchondral SCLEROSIS) → ↓JOINT SPACE → Bone-bone contact
  • PEx: Chronic (>6wks), ↑pain with ACTIVITY, ↓pain w. rest, Morning STIFFNESS* <30 MINS, Crepitus, cold/normal temp, ↓active AND passive ROM, bony deformities (ex. Bouchard's nodes at PIP, Heberden's Nodes at DIP) KNEE > Hip > Hand (including DIP, PIP, and 1st CMC, almost never the MCPs.)!
  • Invx: X-RAYS for staging OA, ↑stage w. ↑osteophytes → Subchondral cysts → Irregular joint space narrowing → Subchondral SCLEROSIS in STAGE 4 (End-stage). Almost never Invx w. MRI, only if other dx suspected.
    • If warm or swelling → Invx w. Arthrocentesis to rule out infection + gout (Synovial fluid WBC <2,000 in OA)
  • Diagnosis: Mostly CLINICAL. Must have SYMPTOMS (*) + Rule out other dx ± X-ray findings (X-rays alone do not dx)
  • Tx:
    • Non-pharm: ↓weight, exercise (ex. Tai-chi), PT w. "NEUROMUSCULAR" EXERCISE (Best non-pharm tx)...etc.
    • Pharm: Topical or oral NSAIDs. Opioids NOT recommended. Intra-articular steroids (Inconclusive evidence for HA, PRP, stem cells)
    • Surgery (Arthroplasty) if END-STAGE w. ↑↑symptoms + ↓↓QOL. (Note: Arthroscopy has NO meaningful benefit)

nodes.title: Inflammatory Arthritis
nodes.body:
• PEx: Pain w. REST, Morning STIFFNESS >1hr
  • Invx Inflammation: CBC, Plt (↑), Hgb (↓), CRP (↑), ESR (↑)
  • Invx Organ Function: Cr, AST, ALT, Alb, ± Hep B/C.
  • Diagnosis is mostly CLINICAL for all except crystalline arthritis.

nodes.title: Monoarthritis
nodes.body: • Most are ACUTE (<6wks)

nodes.title: Chronic Monoarthritis
nodes.body:
• OSTEOARTHRITIS (Non-Inflamm, most common)
  • GOUT + CPPD/Pseudogout

nodes.title: Crystalline Arthritis
nodes.body:
• Acute intermittent attacks of crystalline arthritis
  • Synovial fluid w. WBC <50,000 + CRYSTALS

nodes.title: Pseudogout
nodes.body:
• ♀♂ (old age)
  • aka. CALCIUM PYROPHOSPHATE DEPOSITION DISEASE (CPPD)
  • Keywords: X-RAY CALCIFICATIONS, KNEE
  • RFs: ↑Age, hyperPTH, hemochromatosis, trauma.
  • Pathophys: ↑CALCIUM or pyrophosphate → Crystallization within articular CARTILAGE and synovial fluid → Inflamm. rxn to crystals.
  • PEx: Acute attacks similar to gout, acute "red, hot, swollen, tender" joint, classically the KNEE (Examine effusion w. PATELLAR BALLOTMENT) ± systemic S/S (ex. fever)
  • Invx: Screen w. X-RAY, showing crystals in cartilage = CHONDROCALCINOSIS!
    • Diagnose w. arthrocentesis showing RHOMBOID-shaped CRYSTALS, (+) birefringence under polarized light (BLUE under parallel light)
  • Tx: Similar to gout but no allopurinol. Often self-limiting.
    • Good HYDRATION important for both.

nodes.title: (Autoimmune) Polyarthritis/Oligoarthritis
nodes.body:
• Invx: RHEUMATOID FACTOR (RF) - An IgM autoantibody against the Fc portion of IgG + X-RAYS to look for EROSIONS.
    • (If unclear PEx, Invx septic arthritis w. arthrocentesis. Rule out w. synovial fluid WBCs 2,000-50,000.)
  • RF may be +ve in other dx: Hep B/C, TB, HIV, Sarcoidosis, Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

nodes.title: Seronegative Polyarthritis aka. Spondyloarthritis
nodes.body:
• ♂ (adults)
  • RFs: Genetics - HLA-B27 +ve (FHx)*
  • PEx: Arthritis involving peripheral + AXIAL joints: SPINE + SI JOINT → Inflammatory BACK PAIN.*
    • ± ENTHESITIS (Inflamm. at tendon-bone insertion ex. Achilles), DACTYLITIS (Inflamm. of digits - "SAUSAGE DIGITS"),* ocular manifestations (e.g. UVEITIS), and constitutional symptoms. Good response to NSAIDs.*

nodes.title: Reactive Arthritis
nodes.body:
• ♂ (adults)
  • Keywords: STDs, YOUNG MEN, DYSURIA, RED EYES
  • Pathophys: Genetic Predisposition (HLA-B27) + Infection - GI (ex. C.diff, Shigella...) or GU (ex. CHLAMYDIA, often in young sex-active men) → 1-3 WEEKS later: Systemic autoimmune reaction
  • PEx: "CAN'T SEE, CAN'T PEE, CAN'T CLIMB A TREE" (Triad of S/S prev. known as "Reiter's Syndrome")
    • Uveitis + Conjunctivitis, Urethritis + Cervicitis (w. dysuria), Enthesitis, dactylitis, sacroiliitis, asymmetric oligoarthritis (LOWER LIMB) and psoriatic-like skin lesions:
      • BALANITIS of the penis
      • KERATODERMA BLENNORRHAGICUM of feet
  • Invx: ↑CRP + ESR. GI/GU infection. Clinical dx.
  • Tx: ABx + manage symptoms (NSAIDs). Can be self-limiting, chronic or progressive.

nodes.title: Psoriatic Arthritis
nodes.body:
• (adults)
  • (Arthritis can occur before or after psoriasis)
  • Keywords: FHx, NAIL DYSTROPHY, SKIN PS.
  • Pathophys: HLA-B27 + FHx of PSORIASIS → ↑IL-6, TNF-α → ↑Autoimmune inflammation to skin, tendons/CT and joints.
  • Skin + Nail PEx: Psoriatic skin PLAQUES (hidden sites ex. umbilicus, scalp...), NAIL DYSTROPHY: PITTING NAIL BEDS, ridging, oil spots.
  • Joints PEx: ASYMMETRIC Oligoarthritis ± DIP (Ray pattern), asymmetric SACROILIITIS
    • Inflamm. EROSIONS → ↑osteoblast act → Deformities: Arthritis Mutilans, "Pencil in cup", Syndesmophytes (large "jug-handle" bridging bone b/w vertebrae)
  • Tendons/CT PEx: Enthesitis, Tenosynovitis or DACTYLITIS aka. "SAUSAGE DIGITS".
    • Periarticular erythema can look PURPLE and be confused w. septic or crystalline arthritis.
    • In Eyes: CONJUNCTIVITIS + UVEITIS (Red eyes!).
  • Invx: ↑CRP, ESR, HLA-B27 +ve. X-RAYS: "PENCIL IN CUP" deformity of DIP, axial syndesmophytes.
  • Tx: NSAIDs + DMARDs (METHOTREXATE...) + Biologics: TNF and IL inhibitors

nodes.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis
nodes.body:
• ♂ (adults)
  • (Ankylos = Joint fusion → Stiffness, Spondy = Vertebrae)
  • Keywords: BAMBOO SPINE, SACROILIITIS, ↓CHEST EXPANSION
  • Pathophys + PEx: HLAB27 + other genes → Autoimmune inflammation begins in SI joint: SACROILIITIS → Erosions on iliac side of SI joint (X-ray w. pseudowidening): Bilateral + symmetric LOW BACK + GLUTEAL PAIN*
    • → Inflamm. ascends up spine → Erosions ↑reactive osteogenesis/sclerosis → Vertebral + SI joint FUSION/ANKYLOSIS → ↓lumbar lordosis ("straight" lumbar spine) and ↑thoracic kyphosis: "?"-shaped column. ↓ROM ex. lumbar flexion (↓ MODIFIED SCHOBER test) → Rigid column / BAMBOO SPINE.
    • Costovertebral/sternal ankylosis → ↓CHEST EXPANSION → Restrictive lung disease.
    • + Systemic Inflammation: Peripheral arthritis*, heel enthesitis*, dactylitis*, uveitis*, psoriasis*, IBD*, Cardiac (AORTITIS), renal (amyloidosis), etc.
  • Invx: X-RAYS - SI joint erosion ± sclerosis, vertebral fusion ("BAMBOO SPINE"). → MRI is more sensitive for early disease (nr-axSpA). ↑ESR + CRP.
  • Diagnosis: ≥3 months back pain, age at onset <45 y.o AND one of:
    • Sacroiliitis on imaging + ≥1 SpA feature (*)
    • HLA-B27 + ≥2 other SpA features (*)
  • Tx: PT, NSAIDs (INDOMETHACIN), Biologics: TNF-INHIBITORS, IL-17 inhib.
    • (Note: DMARDs do NOT work for spinal S/S)!

nodes.title: Enteropathic Arthritis
nodes.body:
• aka. IBD-ASSOCIATED
  • (Review PoM I - GI: IBD)
  • PEx: IBD symptoms + PEx of SpA. If initial dx - need to rule out Septic arthritis (may also present w. abdominal pain, diarrhea, bleed...)

nodes.title: Seropositive Polyarthritis
nodes.body:
• ♀
  • If you suspect RA based on PEx: Invx: ANTI-CCP (ANTI-CYCLICAL CITRULLINATED PROTEIN)
  • If you suspect CT dx based on PEx: Invx: ANA (ANTI-NUCLEAR ANTIBODY) (Stronger results have large denominators ex. 1/1200)
  • +ANA: Many false positives. Sensitive + non-specific Invx

nodes.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
nodes.body:
• ♀ (old age)
  • Keywords: ↑ with REST, MCP and PIP in both hands
  • Pathophys: Genetics + triggers (ex. infection, SMOKING) → Inflammation (TNFα, IL-6, CRP...) + Autoantibodies (RF, Anti-CCP...) → Synovitis and EFFUSION = Joint SWELLING and stiffness. → Synovial membrane angiogenesis + hyperplasia → Lumps. "BOGGY" joints
    • → Inflamed synovium secretes lytic enzymes → Destroys cartilage = ↓joint space, BONE DESTRUCTION = Osteopenia and EROSIONS → ↓ROM, deformities (ex. Mal-align, SUBLUXATIONS). → Untreated: systemic inflammation → Extraarticular manifestations.
  • PEx: ↑pain with REST, ↓pain w. activity. Morning STIFFNESS >60 MINS, ↓Active ROM, Pain at NIGHT, Cardinal signs of inflamm. (SWELLING, warm, tender but NOT red). CONSTITUTIONAL S/S (FATIGUE + SLEEP disturbances most common)
    • EXTRA-ARTICULAR manifestations (ex. RA NODULES, ILD, pleural effusions...), Joint DEFORMITIES (ex. Swan Neck), malalignment (late), SYMMETRIC joint involvement - "loves SMALL JOINTS" (Ankles, wrists, MCPs and PIP but SPARES THE DIP JOINT)!
  • Invx: ↑CRP + ESR, ↑Plt, ↓Hgb. X-RAY (findings in later stages of RA): Soft tissue swelling, EROSIONS, joint space narrowing, malalignment (ex. MCP SUBLUXATION, ulnar deviation), OSTEOPENIA
  • Autoantibody: RF, Anti-CCP (More specific to RA) - -ve RF, -Anti-CCP, -ANA do NOT rule out RA. RF predicts prognosis (↑ w. Erosions on X-ray) RF not useful to follow titres (Not predictive of flares)
  • Diagnosis: Mostly CLINICAL.
  • Tx: NSAIDs, Celecoxib → Medium dose Prednisone for flares → DMARDs (1st line: METHOTREXATE!) → If persistent: Biologics (TNF-α inhibitors / Infliximab)

nodes.title: Connective Tissue Disorder Associated Polyarthritis
nodes.body:
• (SLE is more common, other three are rare dx)
  • Screen w. RF and ANA, if +ve + clinical suspicion of SLE: Invx: ANTI-dsDNA (and Anti-Smith on ENA)
  • Screen w. RF and ANA, if +ve + clinical suspicion of CT dx, refer so that specialist can order: Invx: ENA PANEL (EXTRACTABLE NUCLEAR ANTIGEN)
    • ENA w. Anti-Ro/Anti-La → Sjögren
    • ENA w. Anti-Jo1 + ↑CK in Serum → Polymyositis + Dermatomyositis
    • ENA w. Anti-Scl70 ± Anti-Centromere → Scleroderma

nodes.title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
nodes.body:
• ♀ (adults)
  • (May be non-systemic: CUTANEOUS LUPUS)
  • Keywords: RASH w. SUN, ORAL ULCERS, ANTI-DNA
  • Pathophys: Genetics (HLA-DR2/3) + triggers (Estrogen, Smoking, UV LIGHT, DRUGS ex. Hydralazine, procainamide, Sulfa ABx) that damage DNA → Type II + III HSR: Autoreactive T-cells (↑IL-6...) + Autoantibodies (ex. ANA, Anti-DNA) → Ab form soluble IMMUNE COMPLEXES that deposit in joints, skin, kidneys → COMPLEMENT activation, inflammation in most body tissues ∴ PEx w. CONSTITUTIONAL S/S (Fatigue, myalgia, WEIGHT LOSS)
  • SKIN PEx: MALAR (Butterfly) RASH* sparing nasolabial folds, rash after SUN UV exposure (PHOTOSENSITIVITY),* Discoid Rash* w. scars, mouth/nasal ULCERS, livedo reticularis, vasculitis, RAYNAUD'S, ALOPECIA, only (*) are specific S/S to SLE.
    • Malar Rash not to be confused with ROSACEA (Does not spare the nasolabial folds, and is not often raised)
  • Other PEx: Symmetrical POLYARTHRITIS (NO EROSIONS), CYTOPENIAS
  • Complications: Lupus Nephritis, Infections (due to cytopenia + Tx), PERICARDITIS + pleuritis (beware chest pain in SLE), ↑Thrombosis (APS), Lupus cerebritis, CVD.
  • Invx: ↑CRP + ESR, ↓Plt, ↓Hgb, X-rays show NO erosions (vs. RA erosions).
  • Antibodies: +RF, +ANA + May have +Anti-dsDNA (SLE specific but not sensitive) + Anti-Smith on ENA, ↓C3 and C4 during flares.
    • Note: -ve ANA RULES OUT SLE! but -ve Anti-dsDNA does NOT rule out SLE
  • Note: SLE → Risk for false positive RPR/VDRL (Syphilis Invx)
  • Diagnosis: +ANA ≥1/80 AND ≥10 points on criteria based on PEx (ex. Arthritis = 6 points, Skin lupus = 6), and Invx (ex. low C3 = 3 points, anti-dsDNA = 6).
  • Tx: Lifestyle (↓UV sun, smoking), 1st line: HYDROXYCHLOROQUINE! w. routine EYE exams, ± NSAIDs, low dose steroids, Immunosuppressants (MTX, AZA, MMF), Biologics
    • SLE ↑CVD Risk ∴ monitor + treat HTN, LDL, DM.

nodes.title: Sjögren Syndrome (SS)
nodes.body:
• ♀ (adults)
  • Keywords: DRY EYES + MOUTH, CAVITIES
  • Etiology: 1° (Poorly understood), or 2° to SLE, RA, viral infections... 2° to SLE/RA has ↑arthritis PEx
  • Pathophys: Autoantibodies against EXOCRINE GLANDS (ex. Salivary, lacrimal, skin) + LYMPHOCYTIC infiltration → ↓secretion + Destruction of "moisture" producing glands. (Review PoM I - ENT: Salivary Gland Diseases)
  • PEx: XEROPHTHALMIA (Dry eyes) → Keratoconjunctivitis SICCA. XEROSTOMIA (Dry mouth) → ↑CAVITIES, HALITOSIS (Bad breath). Small vessel vasculitis → PURPURA on lower extremities.
  • Invx: ↑CRP + ESR, ↓WBC (lymphocyte consumption), ↓Hgb
  • Antibodies: +RF, +ANA. Many are + ANTI-RO + ANTI-LA
  • Complications: ↑risk of MALT-LYMPHOMA. Pregnant women w. +Anti-Ro: ↑risk of fetal heart block and NEONATAL LUPUS.
  • Tx: Hydration. Symptom management ex. Eye drops. If severe - steroids, immunosuppression.

nodes.title: Polymyositis + Dermatomyositis
nodes.body:
• ♀ (children) / (old age)
  • Keywords: HIP + SHOULDER MUSCLE WEAKNESS, ↑CK, RASH OVER KNUCKLES
  • Pathophys: Genetics, drugs (ex. statins), NEOPLASM (more likely if older pt. w. dermatomyositis) → Autoantibodies to DNA or RNA in muscle cells → Inflamm. in muscle + skin vasculature → Capillary necrosis → ISCHEMIC MUSCLE DAMAGE (Myositis) → ↑CK.
    • If muscle AND skin affected = Dermatomyositis.
  • PEx: PROXIMAL (HIP + SHOULDER) MUSCLE WEAKNESS + PAIN (Myalgia).
    • Capillary necrosis in dorsum of hand - GOTTRON PAPULES = rash over KNUCKLES + eyelids (HELIOTROPE RASH), dilated capillaries at the nailbeds, mechanic's hands, photosensitivity w. rash in chest "SHAWL and V SIGN"
  • Invx: ↑CREATININE KINASE (CK)!, ± ↑ESR, ↑Aldolase, ↑myoglobin, ↑LDH
  • Antibodies: RF, ANA, + Anti-Jo1 associated w. ILD + worse prognosis.
  • Complications: Dysphagia (GI muscles), ASPIRATION (resp muscles), ILD, MYOCARDITIS w. arrhythmias, etc...
  • Tx: HIGH-DOSE PREDNISONE → Steroid-sparing Tx (AZA, MTX...)

nodes.title: Scleroderma
nodes.body:
• ♀ (adults)
  • aka. SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS (SSc)
  • (Review PoM I - ENT: Dysphagia)
  • Keywords: FIBROSIS, DYSPHAGIA, TIGHT SKIN, NAILFOLD CAPILLARIES
  • Pathophys: Unknown triggers → Autoimmune inflammation → Endothelial injury and ↑fibroblast activity (Collagen deposition) → TRIAD OF SSc:
    • AUTOIMMUNITY (Anti-Scl70), VASCULAR INSTABILITY (Raynaud's...), ORGAN FIBROSIS (ex. Skin, ESOPHAGUS/dismotility, lungs/PAH + ILD)
  • SKIN PEx: Thick and tight skin + tendons, ex. in hands = SCLERODACTYLY, pruritus, loss of wrinkles. Damaged DILATED CAPILLARIES under the skin ex. of NAILBEDS, TELANGIECTASIA. Ca2+ deposits in fibrous scar = CALCINOSIS nodules.
    • Other PEx: ALL w. RAYNAUD'S phenom. + GERD ± DYSPHAGIA, digit ulcers.
    • (small orange marks under Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophagus, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia = CREST)
  • Most lethal CT dx due to Pulmonary fibrosis (ILD) + HTN (PAH), CVD, and Renal HTN = SCLERODERMA RENAL CRISIS (↑↑BP) - Tx w. ACEi ❗
  • Subtypes: Limited SSc ("CREST" Syndrome) - more benign. Diffuse SSc (LETHAL)
  • Invx: Mostly clinical dx w. +ANA, + Anti-Scl70 ± Anti-Centromere.
  • Tx: CCBs for Raynaud's, PPIs for GERD, METHOTREXATE for skin fibrosis...
